Sara — great questions, answered inline below. Longer explanation available in the shared benchmark link.

1) Stitching & overlap strategy: we use an overlap + anchor approach: chunk windows with ~512–1024 token overlap, plus anchor prompts that include key metadata (document headers, numbered refs). For extraction tasks we add sentence-level anchors (IDs) so the model can resolve cross-chunk references. Empirically we see a ~12–18% reduction in boundary hallucinations versus naive non-overlap chunking on our benchmark.

2) 64k experiment: we can approximate a 64k run via chunking + stitching; Redwood-Long-32k is optimized for 32k natively — true 64k native support is currently experimental and will be available via our early-access program later this quarter. For the pilot we’ll run a 64k simulation (2x32k with stitching) and measure both ROUGE/BERTScore vs your human summaries. Expect some degradation versus a true single-pass 64k model, but the stitching approach gives predictable failure modes we can mitigate (more overlap, targeted prompts at boundaries).

3) Cost estimate (rough): for a 50-doc run (avg 80k tokens/doc)
   - Redwood-Long-32k (stitching): ~120k total tokens per doc processed (overlap/stitching) => ~6M tokens total; estimated compute cost: $X (we’ll provide precise quote after we pick run config)
   - Redwood-Standard-8k (chunk & compress): higher orchestration overhead, lower per-token model cost; quality is expected to be lower for cross-ref fidelity.

Dylan — can you confirm we can kick off the harness run on Wednesday once Sara approves the sample set? I’ve attached the initial eval runs from our internal sanity tests.

Marissa
